main_text.p: volentem mutilare. Neque enim defensio corporis tantum in mortis consistit propulsatione, sed etiam vulnerum aversione. Cùm etiam ad vulnera, quæ ad mensuram non infliguntur, ad membri amputationem mors nonnunquam subsequatur.

Idem suadent, omnes illæ rationes Scripturariæ, quibus necessariam defensionem etiam in conscientiæ foro licitam esse demonstrabatur. Neque in contrarium suader[?],quod leges loquantur de periculo mortis avertendo; ut si tale periculum non sit, nec videatur aggressor licitè necari. Respondeo enim, quia intentioni lædentis, non semper respondet eventus, neque vulnera ad modum infliguntur, ideo adversus eum, qui vulnerare voluit, tanquam adversus aggressorem iniquum & latronem nof-

page.notes: Blots and ink specks are visible in the text block, at "etiam" (line 3), before "esse" (ink mark), and at "ideo" (ink blot over "ideo"); they are not printed text and are not transcribed. "suader,quod": the word after "suader" is read as printed; the final letter is uncertain and marked [?]. Long s is rendered as s throughout. Line-end hyphen in "nof-" is printed and kept; the continuation lies on the next page. The bottom of the page carries no catchword.
